According to the USPTO, strong, highly registerable marks are creative or unique names that set a brand apart. These include fanciful marks (made-up words like Pepsi), arbitrary marks (unrelated real words like Apple for computers), and suggestive marks (words hinting at a quality without stating it outright like Coppertone). Conversely, weak or unacceptable marks are hard to protect and usually cannot be federally registered. These include descriptive marks (merely detailing a feature or quality, like Creamy for yogurt) and generic terms (the common, everyday product name, like Bagel shop).
On average across every mark the Company plans to apply for, how descriptive are they on a scale of 1–5? Please rate them with 1 being a weak mark that concisely describes a feature or quality of the goods or services, and 5 being a strong mark that has no relationship to what the Company is selling.
